title: ALL-IN meta-analysis: breathing life into living systematic reviews and prospective meta-analyses
extended_summary:
This paper proposes ALL-IN meta-analysis (Anytime Live and Leading INterim meta-analysis), a statistical framework for evidence synthesis that can be updated continuously as new trial data arrive. The authors argue that conventional meta-analyses and living systematic reviews often suffer from accumulation bias and type-I error problems when analyses are updated after seeing results, especially if the number of studies or interim looks was not fixed in advance.

The central contribution is a betting-score/e-value approach that converts individual trial results into likelihood ratios that can be multiplied across studies and across interim updates. The framework is presented as valid for both retrospective and prospective meta-analysis, and for completed studies as well as interim data from ongoing studies, without requiring prespecified stopping rules or a maximum sample size. The paper uses COVID-19 vaccine trials as illustrative examples, including Pfizer/BioNTech and CureVac, to explain the method in the language of betting, likelihood ratios, and anytime-valid confidence intervals.

The paper is methodological rather than an empirical education study, so it does not involve students, teachers, or schools. Its conclusions are that ALL-IN meta-analysis can improve statistical validity, efficiency, collaboration, and communication in evidence synthesis by allowing analyses to be updated at any time while maintaining frequentist error control. The authors position this as a more flexible alternative to existing living systematic review and prospective meta-analysis approaches that depend on outside control, fixed sample sizes, or enforced stopping rules.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a methodological/statistical theory paper about ALL-IN meta-analysis, not an empirical study of an education intervention. It does not evaluate student, teacher, or school outcomes in K-12 settings.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational intervention effect is estimated, so there is no measurable impact on learning or implementation outcomes to code.
